before.name: sign_in_and_focus_quality
before.description:
Require a polished sign-in treatment with programmatically labelled email and
password fields, understandable invalid-login feedback, practical control
sizes, and clearly visible keyboard focus for fields, buttons and links. After
sign-in, identity and sign-out must be understandable without relying on color
or placeholder text alone.

Rate 1 when labels, feedback or keyboard focus are missing enough to obstruct
sign-in or sign-out; 3 when the full flow is understandable and operable but
focus contrast, control sizing or feedback placement is inconsistent; 5 when
all listed fields/actions have clear names, visible focus, comfortable sizing
and immediately understandable success/error/identity feedback. Use 2 or 4
for intermediate quality, citing the observed strengths and defects.

after.name: sign_in_and_focus_quality
after.description:
Setup: inspect the signed-out form at desktop and 375 by 760, then sign in as Polly through the visible UI.
Graded observations:
1. Email, password, sign-in and sign-out have programmatic names; invalid-login feedback is understandable.
2. Real keyboard traversal gives fields, buttons and links visible focus without a trap. Controls have practical touch targets at the required mobile width.
3. Signed-in identity and sign-out are understandable without colour or placeholder text alone.
Grade operability and understandable feedback, not palette, typography or decorative styling.

disposition: Interaction observations retained as binary; aesthetics moved to Visual

before.name: responsive_shell_and_touch_targets
before.description:
At exactly 375 by 760 pixels, require the public sign-in surface and, after
sign-in, the canvas, visible game controls and leaderboard region to remain
reachable without horizontal page overflow, clipped labels or overlapping
controls. Inputs and visible action controls must remain practical touch
targets. All listed surfaces are required; do not waive a missing canvas,
game control region or leaderboard and then award full credit.

Rate 1 when a required main surface is missing, unreachable or substantially
clipped/overlapping; 3 when every listed surface is reachable and the main
actions work but minor clipping, cramped targets or awkward spacing remains;
5 when every listed surface is usable with no horizontal page overflow,
clipped labels or overlaps and action targets can be selected comfortably.
Use 2 or 4 for intermediate quality. Inspect both signed-out and signed-in UI.

disposition: Presentation moved to six reference Visual axes; mobile operability retained in Polish

before.name: visual_shell_hierarchy
before.description:
At desktop and mobile sizes, require an intentional arcade identity, consistent
spacing, legible typography, purposeful high-contrast color, coherent panels,
and clear visual priority between heading, identity, canvas, controls and
leaderboard. This criterion judges the rendered shell only and does not award
credit for gameplay that is absent.

Rate 1 for unreadable text or hierarchy so flat/crowded that heading, identity,
game, actions and records cannot be located; 3 for a readable arcade shell
with those regions identifiable but inconsistent spacing, typography or panel
grouping; 5 for legible high-contrast text, consistent spacing/type/panels and
clear priority among every listed region on desktop and mobile. Use 2 or 4
between anchors. Accept any coherent arcade theme, not a prescribed palette.

disposition: Presentation moved to six reference Visual axes; mobile operability retained in Polish

before.name: semantic_game_state_and_events
before.description:
Require a focusable named canvas with a useful state summary, semantic DOM
identity and all six HUD values (score, lives, level, combo, active power-up
and timer), named game controls, visible keyboard
guidance, exposed Assist state, revision/sync text, readable mechanics
telemetry, recent events and semantic personal history. Live status and events
must clearly update for sign-in, launch, pause and an exercised lab outcome
without relying on canvas pixels.

after.name: semantic_game_state_and_events
after.description:
Setup: sign in as Polly, use the visible ranked-run controls and a non-scoring lab drill, and inspect the ordinary DOM state alongside the canvas.
Graded observations:
1. A named focusable canvas has a useful state summary. Ordinary DOM exposes identity and all six HUD values: score, lives, level, combo, active power-up and timer.
2. Controls are named, keyboard guidance is visible, Assist state and revision/sync state are understandable, and mechanics telemetry, recent events and personal history are readable as text.
3. Status and events update for sign-in, launch, pause and the exercised lab outcome without requiring canvas-pixel interpretation. This checks semantic communication, not exact physics already graded in Functional.

disposition: Interaction observations retained as binary; aesthetics moved to Visual

before.name: keyboard_pointer_touch_gameplay
before.description:
On a fresh ready run, verify pointer movement and keyboard Left/Right both move
the paddle and its waiting ball smoothly. Space launches; P and Escape toggle
pause/resume. At a touch-sized viewport, touch-equivalent dragging over the
canvas and the large visible action controls remain practical. Input must not
scroll the page unexpectedly, trap focus, or become unusable after reload.

after.name: keyboard_pointer_touch_gameplay
after.description:
Setup: as Polly start a fresh ready run through the visible controls. Repeat input observations at 375 by 760 using the app's supported touch controls.
Graded observations:
1. Pointer and Left/Right both move the paddle and waiting ball; Space launches; P and Escape toggle pause/resume.
2. Touch-equivalent dragging over the canvas and the large visible action controls remain practical and reachable.
3. Input does not unexpectedly scroll the page or trap focus, and remains usable after an ordinary reload and supported return to the game.
Judge usable input and focus, not motion aesthetics or a particular layout.

disposition: Interaction observations retained as binary; aesthetics moved to Visual

before.name: canvas_and_state_readability
before.description:
Require clear HUD priority and a canvas that keeps paddle, balls, falling
items, normal/strong/damaged/solid bricks, overlays and controls easy to
distinguish at desktop and mobile sizes. Brick durability and item type must
not depend on color alone, and the semantic state summary must agree with the
visible scene.

Rate 1 when the scene or HUD is unreadable, major object types are absent or
indistinguishable, or the semantic summary contradicts play; 3 when the scene
and HUD are usable and broadly agree but damaged/solid bricks, drops or
overlays remain difficult to distinguish in some states/sizes; 5 when every
listed object/state is legible at both sizes, durability/item identity has
non-color cues, HUD priority is clear and summary matches the scene. Use 2 or
4 for intermediate quality. Inspect Brick types and Power relay to expose
the required object states instead of assuming unseen ones are correct.

after.name: canvas_and_state_readability
after.description:
Setup: use the visible Brick types and Power relay non-scoring drills to expose the relevant scene states at desktop and 375 by 760.
Graded observations:
1. Brick durability and item type have non-colour cues, so normal, intact/damaged strong, solid bricks and the available power-up types can be identified without colour alone.
2. Ordinary semantic state summaries agree with the scene states actually observed; overlays and control labels do not contradict the displayed phase.
Typography, scene composition and colour treatment are assessed by Visual. Do not invent unseen gameplay outcomes or duplicate the exact drill totals from Functional.

disposition: Interaction observations retained as binary; aesthetics moved to Visual

before.name: complete_product_coherence_and_reduced_motion
before.description:
Confirm sign-in, level selection, saved-run choice, canvas, HUD, controls,
effect timer, sync state, mechanics lab, seed manifest, live feedback, run
history, leaderboard, restart and sign-out feel like one finished arcade
product. Exercise a fresh run, pause/resume, one deterministic drill and reload;
require understandable feedback, stable rendering and no fatal console error,
broken glyph, debug residue or control that contradicts the visible phase.
Emulate reduced motion and require nonessential transition/animation durations
to be materially shortened while the page remains coherent and usable.

Rate 1 when the listed journey is broken or disconnected, errors prevent
completion, or missing feedback leaves the current phase unusable; 3 when
the journey completes with understandable phases but some sync/lab/history
transitions have inconsistent feedback or distracting motion; 5 when every
listed region participates coherently, feedback agrees with phase, there are
no fatal errors/broken glyphs/debug residue, and reduced motion materially
shortens nonessential effects without losing information. Use 2 or 4 for
intermediate quality. An app with no nonessential animation already satisfies
the reduced-motion aspect. Do not collapse one minor flaw into a score of 1.

after.name: complete_product_coherence_and_reduced_motion
after.description:
Setup: as Polly complete an ordinary fresh-run, pause/resume, one non-scoring drill and reload journey through the visible UI.
Graded observations:
1. Sign-in, level selection, saved-run choice when a save exists, controls, effect timer, sync feedback, lab, seed manifest, history, leaderboard, restart when available and sign-out communicate their current state and available actions.
2. The exercised journey has understandable feedback, no fatal browser error or unusable phase, and no visible control that contradicts the current phase.
3. Under reduced-motion preference, nonessential transitions/animations are materially shortened without losing information. An app with no nonessential animation already satisfies this part.
Judge usable feedback and motion preference support, not decorative coherence, which belongs in Visual.

disposition: Interaction observations retained as binary; aesthetics moved to Visual
